newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's NBD pays out 1.5 pounds dividend. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Egypt's NBD pays out 1.5 pounds dividend. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]

text.p: Egypt's mostly-private National Bank for Development/NBD has said it would pay out 1.5 pounds ($0.44) per share for calendar 1996. (Corrects from "1.5 per share")
The bank said in its annual general meeting earlier this week that it had decided to postpone its capital increase by 50 million pounds until the government sold its 30 percent stake in the bank.
The postponement was aimed at avoiding a swamp of bank shares on the market and the subsequent fall in share price. The share last traded on the stock exchange at 24.65 pounds.
Brokers made the meeting's details available to Reuters.

NBD said in statements distributed during the meeting that it made 30.888 million pounds profit in 1996, up from 24.669 million in 1995. It had shareholders' equity worth 242.8 million pounds in 1996, up from 152.717 million pounds.
NBD's capital in the financial year ending on December 31, 1996 was 150.684 million pounds. Its shares have a nominal value of 10.00 pounds.
